source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Only after delivery, with no antepartum dosing at all, similar to what the client is currently assuming about the timing of this medication","B":"Only in the first trimester, with no further dosing, which does not describe the actual typical timing of this medication during pregnancy","C":"Never during pregnancy, only in the postpartum period, similar to the client's current assumption about when this medication is given","D":"Around 28 weeks gestation, plus postpartum if indicated, rather than only after delivery as the client is currently assuming"}}
source_row.rationale: Rho(D) immune globulin is typically administered to Rh-negative pregnant clients at approximately 28 weeks gestation as a standard antepartum dose, in addition to a postpartum dose if the newborn is confirmed Rh-positive, and after any event with potential fetal-maternal blood exposure (such as amniocentesis, trauma, or vaginal bleeding), to help prevent maternal Rh sensitization.

source_row.source_name: ACOG — Rh(D) Immune Globulin Administration Timing
source_row.stem: A nurse is caring for an Rh-negative pregnant client, and the client assumes Rho(D) immune globulin (RhoGAM) is only ever given right after delivery if needed, with nothing required earlier in the pregnancy. RhoGAM is typically instead administered at approximately which point during pregnancy, in addition to after delivery if the newborn is Rh-positive?
